target_customer: Financial institutions, first credit unions, now enterprises that want to control how AI models describe them
problem: Enterprises lack a verified source of truth for AI agents and answer engines; early on, credit unions lacked a way to answer member and staff questions from their documents.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for knowledge bases and generative engine optimization
product_category: Enterprise knowledge base and GEO platform

founders.name: Saroop Bharwani
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a tech entrepreneur; no employers or education given.

founders.name: Thomas Nelson
education: Background in computer science and neuroscience (degree not stated on the YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval and knowledge base infrastructure for regulated customers; standard LLM engineering at the time with compliance and integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Customers load their verified documents and integrations, but retrieval stacks were widely available in early 2024.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: General purpose LLM vendors and search incumbents could ship document Q and A. In October 2026 Zeta Global agreed to acquire Senso, whose tech already powered Zeta's GEO product.

market_need_then: Credit unions and banks wanted accurate answers from their own documents; by 2025 enterprises worried about how AI answer engines represent them, creating the GEO category (the company launched a GEO tool in 2025 per BetaKit).

identity.visual_style: Clean modern product mockups and a developer CLI snippet (company site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Authoritative, trust focused: 'Own The Trusted AI Answer'

brand_strength.rationale: Short and distinctive but resembles other Senso or Sensei names; no press on the brand itself.

pivots.to: Company founded; later moved to knowledge base
AI knowledge base for credit unions

outcome_analysis: Senso started in 2017 selling retention analytics to financial institutions, nearly did not survive by 2022 according to its CEO, then joined YC in 2024 and rode the GEO wave. In October 2026 Zeta Global agreed to acquire it after its technology already powered Zeta's GEO offering; the price is undisclosed and the deal was announced, not shown as closed.
notes: Directory status is Active while Zeta announced an agreement to acquire in October 2026; close not confirmed, so exit type is recorded as acquisition announced. The 2019 seed amount is quoted as 1.5 million Canadian dollars in the headline and about 1.1 million in total seed per Crunchbase News, so amount_usd is null. Pre-YC rounds predate the batch. A $500K 2024 round appears only in aggregators (VCBacked, StartupIntros, CB Insights with conflicting dates) and is unverified. YC lists founded 2024 but BetaKit says 2017. No dated competitors near the batch were found; GEO competitors found were dated 2025 or later.
